answer.evidence: The main body is a sign panel (rows 0-14, width 10) on a thin pole (rows 15-27, width 4) and a small base (rows 28-31). The panel's cream band at rows 1-3 is a face-on header. It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse, and it widens only by the outline row 0 (width 8 to 10). The rest of the panel is a teal stripe with a white ring and a gold field with a number, all vertical face. The base shows only a 1-2 row lighter strip at rows 29-30, which is a rim and not a real top surface. Nothing in the drawing shows a horizontal surface seen from above, so it reads as a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin sign-on-pole prop. It has 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 6 for bus-shelter-a, 12 for kiosk-a and 20 for vending-a. Near-flat coverage is 0%, below bus-shelter-a's 9% and level with kiosk-a and vending-a. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted. By eye it is a dark blue-grey/brown tone beside the yellow sign head and the grey pole, not a uniform black sticker line. The sign face has a highlight, a mid tone and a dark symbol, and the pole and base carry a few tone steps. Shading is a little shallower than vending-a, but it is level with kiosk-a and bus-shelter-a. A careful artist would accept it next to these references without it looking flatter or thinner.
